summary:
Method and limits. I opened the primary URLs (arXiv abstract and HTML pages, GitHub READMEs, Hugging Face cards, PyPI), read the NXAI licence text, and read the project's own LOG.md rows, T01/T03/T05/T10/T12/T13 reports and the 2026-10-11 and 2026-10-17 research notes in the nt-tactical checkout. For installs I ran pip dry-run resolutions (cross-targeted to win_amd64, binary-only, `--report`) in throw-away folders on D: that I deleted afterwards. I installed nothing, downloaded no weights and did not touch the nt env or any repo. Runtime behaviour on Windows is therefore untested everywhere. GitHub API quota ran out after 12 repos, so a few star/last-push figures (TSLib, neuralforecast, AutoGluon, MAPIE, ts2vg repos) were not re-checked. All benchmark numbers in the papers are the authors' own.

Biggest corrections to the catalogue
1. Kronos is less contaminated than our notes say. The paper states pretraining data run up to June 2024 and the test starts July 2024. Clean windows are 2024-07-01..2025-07-20 in the cut file and the Binance forward file 2025-10..2026-09. Anything earlier is contaminated. The repo is stale (last push 2026-04-13), not on PyPI, and the headline numbers use Kronos-large, which is not open.
2. Brini 2607.05291 (cited by most sub-reports) does not test Chronos-2, TiRex or Kronos. It tests Chronos-Bolt, Moirai 2.0, Moirai-MoE, Lag-Llama, TimesFM 2.5, Toto, Sundial and TTM on DAILY horizons (1, 5, 22 days) of 5-minute RV. Only TTM beats Log-HAR, by 1.3-1.8% QLIKE. There is no evidence about next-hour or 1-minute crypto.
3. arXiv 2608.08825 (RF-corrected frozen TimesFM, correlation 0.597) predicts opening-hour stock returns, not volatility, and the figure looks too high to trust. It cannot support the residual-stacking claim.
4. The Chronos-2 GIFT-Eval win rates in the brief are not in the paper. Table 4 gives 81.9/83.8 (WQL/MASE) against TimesFM-2.5 77.5/77.7 and TiRex 76.5/71.9. Chronos-2's pretraining list has no financial series.
5. Install facts that change the plan:
   - `pip install timesfm[torch]` now gives TimesFM 3.0.2 (non-commercial weights). TimesFM 2.5 is `timesfm==2.0.2`, and its `[xreg]` extra pulls jax[cuda], which is poor on Windows.
   - granite-tsfm 0.3.10 needs Python >=3.11 and torch >=2.10, and IBM says it will not maintain it.
   - TiRex and TiRex-2 are Linux/macOS-tested only, and this machine has no nvcc or MSVC. TiRex-2 exists (NX-AI/tirex-2, Apache-2.0), but the Windows route is Docker, which belongs to the owner's other project.
   - Moirai-2.0 weights are CC-BY-NC-4.0 (11.4M params); uni2ts pins torch<2.5 and numpy 1.26.
   - Toto 1.0 pins exact versions. Toto 2.0 (Python 3.12+, `toto-models`, quantile head) is now the recommended release.
   - tabpfn-time-series 1.3.0 hits pip's resolution-too-deep error and defaults to the cloud client, so data would leave the machine. Use plain `pip install tabpfn` instead; its weights are non-commercial and need a browser login by the owner.
   - ts2vg has no numba dependency. pyts 0.14.0 needs Python >=3.11.
   - neuralforecast hard-requires ray.
6. Overlaps with work we already did:
   - T12 showed monthly isotonic calibration made H3 worse (Brier +3.9%, ECE 3.88 pp). Venn-Abers is isotonic-based, so use long windows or a parametric map.
   - T05 already ran ACI as M5 (coverage sd 0.0014 vs 0.018, about 3.5% interval-score cost).
   - T13 shows support lines help only the next-hour vol-change target, not H3 or range size. Image variants with lines should target vol change.
   - H47's +0.02 over bare HAR vanishes once the network's 60-vector or hourly context is present.
7. Evidence that survives: the Rahimikia, Noguer i Alonso and Goel papers match the brief. ARTEMIS' negative Chronos-2 RankIC on Optiver is real but weak. Haggett's 0.892 AUC is a best-of-eight on a 7-day daily label (ETH 0.492, S&P 0.459). Hajra's SSL thesis probes sector and factor classification, not forecasting.

Verified-installable shortlist (by dry-run resolution; runtime unverified). One consolidated py3.11 env resolves together: chronos-forecasting 2.3.2, timesfm 2.0.2, tirex-ts, visionts, granite-tsfm 0.3.10, mapie, ts2vg, pyts 0.14.0, open_clip_torch (83 packages, torch 2.11.0, transformers 5.20.1). One legacy py3.10 env resolves for Kronos plus Sundial plus faiss-cpu (torch 2.5.1, numpy 1.26.4, transformers 4.40.1, huggingface-hub 0.33.1, pandas 2.2.2). Plain `tabpfn` 9.2.0 resolves cleanly (59 packages). Risky or blocked: TiRex (cuda kernels), TiRex-2, ChatTS, Time-VLM repo, Moirai (NC licence, heavy pins), Toto 1.0.

Recommended bootstrap (the sub-reports' conda-less `python -m venv` and cu121/cu124 indexes would not work):
- Env vars: HF_HOME=D:/nt/nt_mm_cache/hf, TORCH_HOME=D:/nt/nt_mm_cache/torch, PIP_CACHE_DIR=D:/nt/nt_mm_cache/pip, TMP and TEMP=D:/nt/nt_mm_cache/tmp, TABPFN_MODEL_CACHE_DIR=D:/nt/nt_mm_cache/tabpfn, TABPFN_DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1.
- Main env: `C:/Users/Step/miniforge3/Scripts/conda.exe create -y -p D:/nt/nt_mm_env python=3.11`, then `D:/nt/nt_mm_env/python.exe -m pip install torch==2.11.0 torchvision==0.26.0 --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu126`, then `... -m pip install chronos-forecasting "pandas[pyarrow]" "timesfm[torch]==2.0.2" granite-tsfm tirex-ts visionts mapie ts2vg pyts==0.14.0 open_clip_torch tabpfn venn-abers faiss-cpu lightgbm`. The brief named `D:/nt/nt_mm_env` as a venv, but a conda prefix there works the same.
- Legacy env: `conda.exe create -y -p D:/nt/nt_mm_legacy python=3.10`, then torch 2.5.1 from the cu124 index, then `pip install "numpy<2" "transformers==4.40.1" accelerate`, then Kronos's requirements.txt. Clone Kronos into D:/nt/nt_mm_cache/src_kronos.

Additions for the catalogue: FinCast (arXiv 2508.19609, CIKM 2025, ~1B params, Apache-2.0, has a 1-minute crypto zero-shot table where Chronos Small wins at horizon 10; target, test period and cutoff not stated; unverifiable for contamination) and HARNet (arXiv 2205.07719, a CNN initialised to equal HAR, the cleanest 'build on HAR' architecture; daily data). Chronos-2 has `fit()` for full or LoRA fine-tuning, so the residual path and a fine-tuned path are both available. The needs-new-data item stays with the owner (D-050); data.binance.vision has free futures metrics (open interest) from 2020-09-01, monthly fundingRate from 2020-01, and daily bookDepth, which bears on the earlier no-order-book answer.
